newsitem.title: FRANCE: Michelin falls sharply after results.
newsitem.headline: Michelin falls sharply after results.

text.p: Shares in tyremaker Michelin fell sharply on Tuesday after the group reported 1996 results which were below market expectations, brokers said.
Some traders said investors were also disappointed with the dividend, and others said an unexpected risk provision for Michelin's stake in a property bank took the market by surprise.
The stock was down 3.53 percent at 327.60 francs at 1125 GMT, in a market that was down 0.5 percent.
"The market finds these results disappointing. I think the dividend policy was most disappointing. Some people were expecting a bigger increase," a trader said.
Another trader noted that the share has gained more than 20 percent since the start of the year and rose 1.07 percent on Monday ahead of the results.
Michelin reported net attributable profit of 2.89 billion francs, up from 2.80 billion for 1995. The consensus estimate was for a net attributable profit of around 3.4 billion francs.

The results included an 845 million charge, compared with a prior-year exceptional gain of 72 million francs. Some of the exceptionals had been expected, such as the gain from the sale of PSA Peugeot Citroen shares and charges for job cuts in France and Spain.
But the 750 million franc provision for its stake in Banque Industrielle et Mobiliere Privee was a surprise to most analysts.
Michelin set a dividend of 3.40 francs for its A shares, up from 2.85, and a dividend of 3.30 francs for its B shares, up from 2.75.
